title: Head of Software Engineering - Delivery & Operations
description:
CAREERS | SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Head of Software Engineering​
Delivery & Operations
Engineering leadership • Delivery • Organisation

Lead the software engineering organisation and turn ambitious technical priorities into
predictable, high-quality delivery.

ABOUT NEURASPACE

Neuraspace is a European space technology company building intelligent solutions for safer, more
autonomous and more resilient space operations. Our platform combines space domain awareness,
automation, artificial intelligence and multi-source data to support satellite operators, institutional
customers and defence users in making faster, better-informed operational decisions. As space becomes
more congested, contested and complex, our ambition is clear: to help define how space operations are
conducted in the age of autonomy.
We are growing our engineering organisation and are looking for a Head of Software Engineering – Delivery
& Operations to take overall accountability for the organisation, execution and delivery of our software
engineering function.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a senior engineering leadership role at the intersection of software engineering, delivery, people
leadership, operational execution and space operations.
You will be accountable for the overall functioning of the Software Engineering organisation: ensuring that
teams are structured effectively, priorities are translated into executable plans, ownership is clear,
dependencies are managed, resources are aligned and commitments are delivered predictably.
You will work in close partnership with the Head of Software Engineering – Architecture & Technology, who
owns the technical integrity, architecture and long-term evolution of the software estate. Delivery &
Operations owns the organisation and its execution; Architecture & Technology owns the technical integrity
of what the organisation builds.
Together, the two Heads ensure that Neuraspace delivers software that is both technically sound and
delivered predictably. Neither architecture nor delivery is optimised in isolation.
This role is not simply about tracking deadlines. You will be expected to understand software engineering
deeply enough to challenge plans, identify risks, make informed trade-offs and work credibly with senior
engineers and architects.
A strong understanding of the space domain and satellite operations environment is essential. You should
be able to connect engineering execution to mission needs, flight dynamics, operational constraints and the
realities of delivering systems used in space operations.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 •​ Lead the Software Engineering organisation from an operational and delivery perspective.
 •​ Own software engineering planning, delivery cadence, milestones, commitments and execution.
 •​ Translate company, product and technical priorities into executable engineering plans with clear
  ownership, sequencing and deadlines.
 •​ Ensure that delivery commitments are realistic, understood and actively managed.
 •​ Maintain clear visibility of progress, risks, dependencies, blockers and resource needs, and drive timely
  escalation and resolution.
 •​ Ensure that responsibilities and decisions are clearly assigned and followed through.
 •​ Establish effective delegation and prevent unnecessary concentration of knowledge, responsibility or
  decision-making in individual people.
 •​ Coordinate closely with Backend, Frontend, MLOps, Product, Flight Dynamics, AI, data and other
  technical teams.
 •​ Work with Team Leads to manage workload, staffing, capacity and prioritisation.
 •​ Own the operational interface between Software Engineering and Product, and coordinate engineering
  input into company-level planning and commitments.
 •​ Establish pragmatic engineering-management practices covering planning, execution tracking, delivery
  reviews, reporting and retrospectives.
 •​ Improve predictability and execution discipline without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.
 •​ Provide management with transparent, timely and decision-useful visibility of engineering performance.
 •​ Own engineering resource planning and contribute to hiring priorities.
 •​ Lead or coordinate people-management processes across Software Engineering and support Team
  Leads in delegation, feedback, performance management and team development.
 •​ Ensure sufficient documentation, knowledge sharing and operational continuity across the organisation.
 •​ Coordinate incident response and operational escalation where engineering organisation and
  prioritisation are required.
 •​ Work with the Head of Software Engineering – Architecture & Technology on technical feasibility,
  architectural constraints and engineering trade-offs.
 •​ Co-own release readiness where technical quality and delivery commitments intersect.
 •​ Ensure software engineering decisions remain grounded in the realities of satellite missions, SDA and
  operational use.
 •​ Support recruitment, onboarding and development of engineering talent and help shape the
  organisation as Neuraspace scales.

DECISION RIGHTS

This role is accountable for:
 •​ Engineering priorities, sequencing, delivery plans and commitments.
 •​ Team organisation, resource allocation, staffing and capacity planning.
 •​ Engineering processes, cadence, ownership and delegation.
 •​ Cross-team dependencies, escalation and delivery reporting.
 •​ Operational coordination with Product and other company functions.
 •​ Overall functioning of the Software Engineering organisation.
 •​ Jointly with Architecture & Technology: roadmap feasibility, major technical-versus-delivery trade-offs,
  release readiness, technical-debt prioritisation and senior technical hiring.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who combines strong software engineering foundations, engineering
leadership, delivery discipline, organisational capability and solid space-domain experience.
 •​ Significant professional experience in software engineering, including technically complex systems.
 •​ Previous senior responsibility for engineering teams, software delivery or engineering operations.
 •​ Demonstrated experience leading multiple engineers, teams or technical workstreams.
 •​ Strong ability to translate priorities into structured, executable plans and improve delivery predictability.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Strong planning and organisational skills with a disciplined approach to commitments and deadlines.
 •​ Experience managing cross-team dependencies, competing priorities and limited resources.
 •​ Ability to engage credibly with senior engineers and architects while maintaining focus on execution.
 •​ Strong understanding of modern software engineering practices, architectures and development
  lifecycles.
 •​ Experience with engineering capacity planning, staffing and prioritisation.
 •​ Experience mentoring engineering managers, Team Leads or senior engineers.
 •​ A pragmatic approach to engineering processes: enough structure to improve predictability and quality
  without unnecessary overhead.
 •​ Strong communication skills and the ability to create clarity across technical and non-technical
  stakeholders.
 •​ A high level of ownership and the ability to make and drive decisions.
 •​ Professional experience in the space sector and a solid understanding of satellite operations.
 •​ Familiarity with one or more of the following: satellite operations, flight dynamics, mission control,
  ground segments, SDA, space surveillance or spacecraft operations.
 •​ Professional fluency in English.

WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU STAND OUT

 •​ Experience as a Head of Engineering, Engineering Manager, Director of Engineering, Delivery Lead or
  Technical Programme Lead.
 •​ Experience delivering mission-critical, safety-critical or high-availability software.
 •​ Experience in Space Traffic Management, Space Domain Awareness, Flight Dynamics or satellite mission
  operations.
 •​ Experience in defence, aerospace or other complex operational environments.
 •​ Experience scaling or professionalising an engineering organisation through rapid growth.
 •​ Experience working across software, data, AI/ML and operational technology teams.
 •​ Familiarity with cloud-native architectures, distributed systems and data-intensive platforms.
 •​ Familiarity with secure software development environments and systems for institutional or defence
  customers.
 •​ Experience managing distributed or multi-site engineering teams.

HOW WE WORK

At Neuraspace, engineering is closely connected to the operational problems we solve. Our teams work
across software engineering, artificial intelligence, flight dynamics, data, space surveillance and satellite
operations. We value technical depth, but equally value people who can turn good engineering into reliable
operational capability.
The Head of Software Engineering – Delivery & Operations and the Head of Software Engineering –
Architecture & Technology form the leadership pair for Software Engineering. The two roles are expected to
work closely, openly and constructively, with clear decision rights and shared responsibility for the overall
success of the engineering organisation.
We expect leaders to create clarity, take ownership, communicate openly and help others succeed.

WHY NEURASPACE

 •​ Take overall operational leadership of Software Engineering in a growing European space technology
  company.
 •​ Shape how our engineering organisation plans, executes and scales.
 •​ Build strong delivery discipline without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
 •​ Work on software used in real satellite operations and Space Domain Awareness.
 •​ Work alongside experienced software engineers, architects, Flight Dynamics specialists, AI experts and
  space professionals.
 •​ Influence organisational structure, engineering processes, hiring and leadership development.
 •​ Contribute to systems supporting commercial, institutional and defence customers.
 •​ Take meaningful ownership of how Neuraspace turns technical ambition into delivered operational
  capability.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Help build the foundations for increasingly autonomous space operations.

LOCATION

Munich – Germany; Coimbra - Portugal

HOW TO APPLY

APPLICATIONS: Please submit your CV, cover letter and supporting document(s) combined
into one single PDF document. Send your application to jobs@neuraspace.com.

If you are an experienced engineering leader who understands software, understands space and
knows how to turn ambitious technical priorities into a well-organised engineering organisation
that delivers, we would like to hear from you.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

title: Lead MLOps Engineer
description:
CAREERS | AI & SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Lead MLOps Engineer
Production AI • MLOps • Technical leadership

Build, own and grow the MLOps capability powering increasingly autonomous space
operations.

ABOUT NEURASPACE

Neuraspace is a European space technology company building intelligent solutions for safer, more
autonomous and more resilient space operations. Our platform combines space domain awareness,
automation, artificial intelligence and multi-source data to support satellite operators, institutional
customers and defence users in making faster, better-informed operational decisions. As space becomes
more congested, contested and complex, our ambition is clear: to help define how space operations are
conducted in the age of autonomy.
We are expanding our AI and software engineering capabilities and are looking for a Lead MLOps Engineer to
take ownership of our MLOps capability and help build the team and technical foundations required to scale
AI-enabled space operations.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a senior, hands-on technical leadership role at the intersection of machine learning, software
engineering, cloud infrastructure and operations.
You will take ownership of Neuraspace's MLOps capability: designing and building the infrastructure,
tooling and practices required to move AI and machine-learning developments reliably into production,
while remaining directly involved in implementation.
This is not a purely managerial role. You will be expected to contribute hands-on to architecture, code,
deployment pipelines, infrastructure and production operations.
At the same time, you will help shape and grow the MLOps function as Neuraspace scales. You will establish
technical standards, mentor other engineers, support recruitment and onboarding, and progressively build
the team and processes required for a mature production AI environment.
At Neuraspace, machine learning is not an isolated research activity. It is increasingly embedded into
operational systems supporting space domain awareness, anomaly detection, pattern-of-life analysis, data
fusion, automation and decision support.
You will work closely with software engineers, data and AI specialists, Flight Dynamics, Product and
operational teams to ensure that our machine-learning systems are reproducible, scalable, secure and
robust.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 •​ Lead the design and evolution of Neuraspace's MLOps architecture, tooling and operating model.
 •​ Remain hands-on in the development of infrastructure, deployment pipelines, automation and
  production systems.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Design, build and maintain the infrastructure required to develop, deploy and operate machine-learning
  models in production.
 •​ Develop and improve CI/CD pipelines for AI and machine-learning workloads.
 •​ Establish robust processes for model deployment, versioning, validation, promotion and rollback.
 •​ Implement model, data and pipeline observability, including monitoring for performance degradation,
  data drift and operational anomalies.
 •​ Ensure reproducibility across training, validation and production environments.
 •​ Build and maintain tooling for model registries, artefact management and experiment tracking.
 •​ Work closely with AI/ML developers to improve the transition from prototype models to
  production-grade services.
 •​ Integrate machine-learning capabilities into Neuraspace's broader software and data platform.
 •​ Support scalable processing of large and heterogeneous datasets from multiple operational sources.
 •​ Improve infrastructure automation and reduce manual operational overhead.
 •​ Support deployment across cloud, private-cloud, on-premises and secure or restricted environments
  where required.
 •​ Contribute to platform reliability, availability, security and performance.
 •​ Establish appropriate logging, metrics, alerting and tracing for ML-enabled services.
 •​ Define technical standards, patterns and best practices for production AI and MLOps.
 •​ Contribute to architecture decisions concerning AI infrastructure, data pipelines and deployment
  patterns.
 •​ Help ensure that AI-enabled systems meet operational requirements for traceability, explainability and
  reliability.
 •​ Support incident investigation, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement of production ML
  systems.
 •​ Mentor engineers working on MLOps-related topics and help strengthen capability across the wider
  engineering organisation.
 •​ Support the recruitment, onboarding & development of additional MLOps engineers.
 •​ Help define the future structure, responsibilities and operating model of the MLOps team.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who combines strong software engineering foundations, deep practical MLOps
experience and the ability to take technical ownership of a growing capability.
 •​ Significant professional experience in software engineering, DevOps, platform engineering or MLOps.
 •​ Demonstrated experience deploying and operating machine-learning models in production
  environments.
 •​ Strong programming skills, preferably in Python and one or more additional modern programming
  languages.
 •​ Strong understanding of software engineering principles, APIs, distributed systems and production
  environments.
 •​ Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code.
 •​ Experience with containerisation and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
 •​ Experience with cloud platforms and cloud-native architectures.
 •​ Experience with model lifecycle management, experiment tracking and model versioning.
 •​ Experience with observability, monitoring, logging and alerting for production systems.
 •​ Strong understanding of data pipelines, feature pipelines and model-training workflows.
 •​ Familiarity with ML frameworks and the operational challenges associated with deploying them.
 •​ Good understanding of security, access control and software supply-chain considerations.
 •​ Ability to troubleshoot complex distributed production systems.
 •​ Ability to define technical standards and drive their adoption across engineering teams.
 •​ Experience mentoring or technically leading other engineers.
 •​ Strong communication skills and an ability to work effectively across software, AI, data and operational
  teams.
 •​ A high level of ownership and comfort operating in a growing technology organisation.
 •​ Professional fluency in English.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU STAND OUT

 •​ Experience working in the space sector, satellite operations or space domain awareness.
 •​ Experience in aerospace, defence, robotics, autonomous systems or another mission-critical
  environment.
 •​ Experience building an MLOps capability or team from an early stage.
 •​ Experience deploying AI/ML workloads in secure, air-gapped or on-premises environments.
 •​ Experience with real-time or near-real-time ML systems.
 •​ Experience with large-scale time-series, sensor or telemetry datasets.
 •​ Experience with data fusion or heterogeneous sensor data.
 •​ Experience with geospatial or orbital-data applications.
 •​ Familiarity with ML platforms and tooling such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, Argo, DVC or equivalent
  technologies.
 •​ Experience with GPU infrastructure and optimisation of compute-intensive ML workloads.
 •​ Experience with model explainability, validation and governance.
 •​ Experience deploying models at the edge or in resource-constrained environments.
 •​ Experience supporting AI systems used for operational decision-making.

HOW WE WORK

At Neuraspace, AI and machine learning are closely connected to real operational problems. Our teams work
across software engineering, artificial intelligence, flight dynamics, data, space surveillance and satellite
operations. The systems we build must not only perform well in development environments; they must also
operate reliably, transparently and securely in production.
We value pragmatic engineering, technical depth and strong ownership. Leaders at Neuraspace are
expected to remain close to the technology, create clarity, help others succeed and build capabilities that
can scale beyond the individual. We are building towards increasingly autonomous space operations.
Reliable, scalable and production-ready AI is a critical part of making that possible.

WHY NEURASPACE

 •​ Take ownership of the MLOps capability of a growing European space technology company.
 •​ Build the technical foundations for production AI rather than simply operate an established platform.
 •​ Remain deeply hands-on while shaping and growing a technical team.
 •​ Work on AI capabilities used in real space operations and space domain awareness.
 •​ Influence how machine learning is deployed, monitored and scaled across our platform.
 •​ Work alongside software engineers, AI specialists, flight dynamics experts and space professionals.
 •​ Contribute to systems supporting commercial, institutional and defence customers.
 •​ Work on technically demanding problems involving large, heterogeneous and operationally relevant
  datasets.
 •​ Help turn advanced AI capabilities into dependable operational systems.
 •​ Play a central role in building the team, practices and architecture that will support Neuraspace's next
  stage of growth.

LOCATION

 Munich – Germany; Coimbra – Portugal; Wasserbillig – Luxembourg

HOW TO APPLY

APPLICATIONS: Please submit your CV, cover letter and supporting document(s) combined
into one single PDF document. Send your application to jobs@neuraspace.com.

If you are an experienced MLOps engineer who wants to build, own and grow a production AI
capability while remaining hands-on with the technology, we would like to hear from you.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

title: Lead Sensor Systems & Infrastructure Engineer
description:
CAREERS | SENSOR SYSTEMS &
INFRASTRUCTURE

Lead Sensor Systems & Infrastructure
Engineer
Radar Systems • Sensor Infrastructure • Technical Leadership

Own the full lifecycle of radar and ground-based sensing infrastructure — from supplier
and site selection to sustained operations.

ABOUT NEURASPACE

Neuraspace is a European space technology company building intelligent solutions for safer, more
autonomous and more resilient space operations. Our platform combines space domain awareness,
automation, artificial intelligence and multi-source data to support satellite operators, institutional
customers and defence users in making faster, better-informed operational decisions. As space becomes
more congested, contested and complex, our ambition is clear: to help define how space operations are
conducted in the age of autonomy.
We are expanding our sensing and hardware capabilities and are looking for a Lead Sensor Systems &
Infrastructure Engineer to take ownership of the technical and operational lifecycle of Neuraspace’s
ground-based sensing infrastructure.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a senior, hands-on technical leadership role spanning radar systems, sensor engineering, supplier
management, site infrastructure, deployment and operations.
Your initial focus will be strongly centred on radar systems. You will act as Neuraspace’s technical owner for
radar-related developments and as the principal technical interface with radar suppliers and partners.
The role, however, goes considerably beyond the radar itself.
You will own the technical and operational lifecycle of deployed sensing infrastructure: from defining
requirements and assessing suppliers through site identification, infrastructure definition and stakeholder
coordination, to installation, acceptance, commissioning, operations, maintenance and future upgrades.
You will need to understand not only how a radar should perform, but what it takes to turn that radar into a
dependable operational capability: where it can be located, whether the electromagnetic environment is
suitable, what power, communications, civil infrastructure, security and access it requires, which
permissions and clearances are needed, how it integrates with Neuraspace’s systems, how it will be
maintained, and how its real-world performance and availability will be continuously verified.
As Neuraspace expands its sensor network, you will progressively help shape and grow our internal
capability across radar and other ground-based sensing technologies. This is not a purely managerial role.
You will be expected to remain deeply involved in technical analysis, requirements, system reviews,
integration, commissioning, troubleshooting and operational performance.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 •​ Act as Neuraspace’s technical owner for radar systems and associated ground-based sensing
  infrastructure.
 •​ Define system, subsystem, interface, performance and operational requirements, including measurable
  acceptance criteria.
 •​ Translate SDA and operational needs into sensor performance requirements and assess the implications
  for site location, architecture and infrastructure.
 •​ Identify, assess and technically qualify potential radar and sensor suppliers, ensuring that Neuraspace
  maintains sufficient internal expertise to independently assess their solutions.
 •​ Lead technical interfaces with suppliers throughout design, manufacturing, integration, testing,
  deployment, acceptance, operation and upgrade.
 •​ Independently evaluate supplier architectures, technical assumptions, design decisions,
  cost/performance trade-offs and performance claims.
 •​ Lead technical reviews and ensure identified actions, risks and non-conformities are resolved effectively.
 •​ Assess radar performance including detection probability, coverage, sensitivity, measurement accuracy,
  tracking performance, availability and operational constraints.
 •​ Understand and evaluate antennas, RF transmit and receive chains, timing and synchronisation, signal
  processing and associated system interfaces.
 •​ Define and oversee verification and validation activities, including factory and site acceptance testing
  where appropriate.
 •​ Lead the identification and technical assessment of candidate sensor locations, including geometry,
  interference and EMC environment, infrastructure, connectivity, accessibility, security and
  maintainability.
 •​ Define site requirements including electrical power, communications, networking, foundations and civil
  works, environmental protection, physical security, remote access and maintenance access.
 •​ Coordinate with site owners, local authorities, regulators, defence organisations, infrastructure providers
  and other stakeholders required to establish and operate a sensor site.
 •​ Coordinate the technical inputs required for spectrum coordination, frequency licensing, EMC
  assessment and other regulatory or operational clearances.
 •​ Coordinate technical inputs for planning, construction and site-specific approvals, working with legal,
  regulatory, civil-engineering and local specialists as required.
 •​ Oversee installation, system integration, site acceptance, commissioning and entry into operational
  service.
 •​ Ensure reliable integration of sensor data into Neuraspace’s software, data-processing and operational
  platforms.
 •​ Work closely with Space Domain Awareness, Flight Dynamics, software and data teams to understand
  how sensor-level performance translates into tracking, orbit determination and operational outcomes.
 •​ Define operational concepts, maintenance strategies, spares concepts, supplier support arrangements
  and lifecycle plans.
 •​ Monitor availability, data quality and technical performance of deployed sensors and drive corrective
  action where required.
 •​ Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance and manage technical escalation with suppliers.
 •​ Lead technical troubleshooting and root-cause investigations involving hardware, infrastructure and
  interfaces.
 •​ Maintain technical configuration, system documentation, interface definitions, acceptance evidence and
  change control.
 •​ Lead upgrades and performance improvements based on operational experience.
 •​ Support technical make, buy and partner decisions for future sensing infrastructure.
 •​ Contribute to deployment planning for additional radar and other sensor sites.
 •​ Build Neuraspace’s internal sensor-systems and hardware capability, ensuring critical system knowledge
  resides within the company.
 •​ Mentor and help recruit engineers as the capability grows.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who combines deep practical radar expertise, systems engineering capability
and experience turning complex hardware into an operational system.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

•​ Significant professional experience in radar systems engineering, radar technology, RF systems or a
  closely related field.
•​ Hands-on professional experience with real radar systems, including integration, testing, deployment,
  commissioning, operations or maintenance; exclusively theoretical, academic or simulation-based
  experience will not be sufficient for this role.
•​ Experience taking complex hardware or sensor systems from specification through deployment into
  sustained operational use.
•​ Strong understanding of radar principles and system performance.
•​ Experience with radar system architecture, integration, testing, commissioning or operations.
•​ Good understanding of antennas, RF transmit and receive chains, timing, synchronisation and
  signal-processing systems.
•​ Ability to translate operational requirements into technical system and subsystem requirements.
•​ Experience assessing system performance against measurable specifications and acceptance criteria.
•​ Experience working directly with equipment suppliers, technology partners or subcontractors.
•​ Strong systems engineering capability, including requirements, interfaces, verification, configuration
  and change management.
•​ Ability to critically evaluate supplier proposals, designs and performance claims.
•​ Experience troubleshooting complex hardware and integrated systems.
•​ Ability to work effectively across hardware, software, data and operational engineering teams.
•​ Strong organisational skills and the ability to coordinate multiple technical and external stakeholders.
•​ A high level of ownership and comfort operating independently in a growing technology organisation.
•​ Strong communication skills and the ability to represent Neuraspace credibly in technical discussions
  with partners, customers, authorities and suppliers.
•​ Professional fluency in English.

WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU STAND OUT

•​ Space-surveillance radar, SSA or SDA experience.
•​ Experience detecting and tracking orbital objects, particularly in Low Earth Orbit.
•​ Defence, air-surveillance or other high-performance tracking radar experience.
•​ Deployment and commissioning of remote radar installations.
•​ Experience selecting, developing or operating remote sensor sites.
•​ Phased-array radar systems.
•​ Radar calibration and performance characterisation.
•​ Understanding of radar measurements in the context of orbit determination.
•​ Spectrum coordination, frequency licensing and EMC assessment.
•​ Experience working with national authorities, defence organisations or regulatory bodies.
•​ Remote-site infrastructure, civil works, power and communications.
•​ Operation of geographically distributed sensor networks.
•​ Optical or complementary SSA sensor systems.
•​ Multi-sensor fusion.
•​ Secure or defence-grade infrastructure.
•​ Supplier qualification, technical procurement and formal acceptance of complex hardware systems.
•​ Maintenance, availability, spares and lifecycle management of remotely operated systems.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

HOW WE WORK

At Neuraspace, sensors are not standalone pieces of hardware. They are part of an operational system that
turns observations into information and ultimately into decisions. Our teams work across Space Domain
Awareness, Flight Dynamics, software engineering, artificial intelligence, data and satellite operations. The
value of a sensor depends not only on its theoretical performance, but on whether it can be deployed,
integrated, operated and maintained reliably over time.
We therefore value engineers who can move comfortably between system-level thinking and practical
implementation: discussing radar performance in one meeting, site infrastructure in the next, and
operational data quality with the software and Flight Dynamics teams afterwards. We value technical depth,
pragmatism, strong ownership and people who are prepared to take responsibility for making complex
systems work in the real world.

WHY NEURASPACE

 •​ Take technical ownership of Neuraspace’s radar and ground-based sensing infrastructure.
 •​ Build an internal sensor-systems capability rather than simply manage external suppliers.
 •​ Work directly with advanced radar technology and turn it into an operational space-surveillance
  capability.
 •​ Influence supplier selection, system architecture, site deployment and operational concepts.
 •​ Own the complete lifecycle from requirements and procurement through commissioning and long-term
  operations.
 •​ Work closely with Space Domain Awareness, Flight Dynamics, AI, software and operational teams.
 •​ Contribute directly to the expansion of Neuraspace’s independent sensor network.
 •​ Work on systems supporting commercial, institutional and defence customers.
 •​ Remain deeply hands-on while progressively building and leading a technical capability.
 •​ Play a central role in strengthening Neuraspace’s ability to generate and control its own high-quality
  space-surveillance data.

LOCATION

 Munich – Germany; Coimbra – Portugal; Wasserbillig – Luxembourg

HOW TO APPLY

APPLICATIONS: Please submit your CV, cover letter and supporting document(s) combined
into one single PDF document. Send your application to jobs@neuraspace.com.

If you are an experienced radar systems engineer who wants to own the journey from sensor
requirements and supplier selection to site deployment, commissioning and long-term operations
— and build the internal capability that allows Neuraspace to do this at scale — we would like to hear
from you.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
CAREERS | SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Quality Assurance Engineer
Quality engineering • Manual testing • Automation

Embed quality into delivery and build reliable test automation for space operations.

ABOUT NEURASPACE

Neuraspace is a European space technology company building intelligent solutions for safer, more
autonomous and more resilient space operations. Our platform combines space domain awareness,
automation, artificial intelligence and multi-source data to support satellite operators, institutional
customers and defence users in making faster, better-informed operational decisions. As space becomes
more congested, contested and complex, our ambition is clear: to help define how space operations are
conducted in the age of autonomy.

experience in, or a strong interest in, automation to join our engineering team.

This is a hands-on quality engineering role embedded directly within a cross-functional Agile team
developing Neuraspace's Space Traffic Management platform.

Our approach starts with manual testing while features are evolving and introduces automation once
functionality is sufficiently stable. This requires QA Engineers to remain comfortable with both exploratory

 •​ Define test cases and test scenarios for functional, integration and end-to-end testing.
 •​ Perform hands-on functional testing as part of the delivery team.
 •​ Develop and maintain automated end-to-end tests for frontend applications and APIs.
 •​ Help determine when manual test scenarios are mature enough to be automated.
 •​ Support the development team in clarifying requirements and acceptance criteria.
 •​ Identify, document and communicate defects clearly and work with engineers through resolution.
 •​ Support release preparation and verification.
 •​ Contribute to continuous improvement of QA practices, test coverage and automation within the team.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who combines practical testing skills with a structured quality mindset and an
interest in effective automation.
 •​ Practical experience in software quality assurance or software testing.
 •​ Experience with test management tools such as Qase, Xray or equivalent.
  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Experience with Jira and Confluence or equivalent collaboration tools.
 •​ Experience with test automation frameworks such as Playwright, Robot Framework, Cypress or
  equivalent.
 •​ Experience with API testing tools such as Postman or equivalent.
 •​ Experience testing REST APIs.
 •​ Experience with relational databases; PostgreSQL experience is an advantage.
 •​ Ability and willingness to perform manual testing as well as build automation.
 •​ Strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate issues clearly within a cross-functional team.
 •​ Professional fluency in English.

WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU STAND OUT

 •​ Academic background in Software Engineering, Physics, Physics Engineering, Mathematics, Aerospace
  Engineering or another relevant technical field.
 •​ Experience working in the space industry.
 •​ Experience with AWS.
 •​ Two or more years of experience with TypeScript and JavaScript.
 •​ Two or more years of experience with C#.
 •​ Experience with xUnit or NUnit frameworks.
 •​ Experience with unit testing for frontend web applications.
 •​ ISTQB certification.

HOW WE WORK

At Neuraspace, quality is built into delivery. QA Engineers work alongside developers and Product
throughout the development lifecycle rather than testing only at the end.
We value pragmatic testing: use manual testing where it provides speed and insight, automate where
stability and repeatability make automation valuable, and keep improving the balance as the product
evolves.

WHY NEURASPACE

 •​ Work on software supporting real Space Traffic Management and space operations.
 •​ Shape quality practices within a growing European space technology company.
 •​ Work as an integrated member of a cross-functional engineering team.
 •​ Combine hands-on manual testing with meaningful test automation.
 •​ Collaborate closely with software engineers, Product and other technical teams.
 •​ Contribute to systems supporting commercial, institutional and defence customers.
 •​ Help improve the reliability of software used in an increasingly complex space environment.

Munich – Germany; Coimbra – Portugal; Wasserbillig – Luxembourg

title: Requirements Engineer
description:
CAREERS | SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Requirements Engineer
Requirements engineering • Traceability • Verification

Turn complex mission and stakeholder needs into clear, testable and traceable requirements for space
operations.

ABOUT NEURASPACE

Neuraspace is a European space technology company building intelligent solutions for safer, more
autonomous and more resilient space operations. Our platform combines space domain awareness,
automation, artificial intelligence and multi-source data to support satellite operators, institutional
customers and defence users in making faster, better-informed operational decisions. As space becomes
more congested, contested and complex, our ambition is clear: to help define how space operations are
conducted in the age of autonomy.
We are growing our engineering organisation and are looking for a Requirements Engineer to help us
translate operational, customer and business needs into clear, structured and verifiable requirements for
our software-intensive space systems.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This role sits at the interface between customers, users, Product, Software Engineering, Flight Dynamics,
Space Domain Awareness, AI/data teams and programme delivery.
You will help ensure that what Neuraspace builds is based on requirements that are clear, complete,
consistent, traceable and testable. You will work with internal and external stakeholders to understand what
a system needs to achieve, identify constraints and assumptions, resolve ambiguities and translate needs
into requirements that engineering teams can implement and verification teams can test.
This is not a purely administrative requirements-management role. You will be expected to understand the
systems, ask technically meaningful questions, challenge unclear or contradictory inputs, and help teams
distinguish between stakeholder needs, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, interfaces,
constraints and implementation choices.
You will also help create and maintain traceability from customer or mission needs through system and
software requirements to implementation, verification and acceptance.
As Neuraspace increasingly works across commercial, institutional and defence programmes, strong
requirements engineering will be essential to ensuring that complex systems are delivered predictably and
that commitments made to customers are reflected accurately in the systems we build.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 •​ Elicit and analyse requirements from customers, users, Product, technical teams and other stakeholders,
  translating operational needs into clear, structured and verifiable system and software requirements.
 •​ Distinguish between needs, requirements, assumptions, constraints, interfaces and design decisions,
  and ensure requirements are precise, unambiguous, feasible and testable.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Develop and maintain functional and non-functional requirements covering performance, availability,
  reliability, security, usability, interoperability and operational behaviour.
 •​ Identify missing, conflicting or inconsistent requirements and drive their clarification through workshops
  and technical discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
 •​ Support Product and engineering teams in refining features, use cases and acceptance criteria.
 •​ Work closely with Software Engineering, Flight Dynamics, SDA, AI/data and other technical teams to
  ensure requirements are technically understood and correctly decomposed to software, subsystem or
  component level where appropriate.
 •​ Develop and maintain requirements traceability from stakeholder needs through design,
  implementation, verification and acceptance.
 •​ Define and maintain interface requirements together with relevant engineering teams.
 •​ Prepare and maintain system and software requirements specifications, interface documents and related
  technical documentation.
 •​ Support verification and validation planning, ensuring each requirement has an appropriate verification
  method and is linked to test cases, acceptance criteria and evidence.
 •​ Support reviews of requirements, designs and verification results.
 •​ Manage changes to requirements and assess impacts on scope, architecture, implementation, testing,
  schedule and commitments.
 •​ Maintain requirements baselines and contribute to configuration and change-control processes.
 •​ Ensure customer and contractual requirements are correctly flowed down into engineering activities.
 •​ Support proposal and programme teams in analysing tenders, statements of work and customer
  documentation, identifying compliance gaps, technical risks and areas requiring clarification.
 •​ Support acceptance activities by ensuring delivered functionality can be traced back to agreed
  requirements.
 •​ Improve requirements-engineering methods, templates and tooling as Neuraspace grows, promoting
  good practice without unnecessary bureaucracy.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who combines structured analytical thinking, technical understanding, strong
communication skills and the ability to turn complex stakeholder needs into precise engineering
requirements.
 •​ Professional experience in requirements engineering, systems engineering, software engineering,
  business analysis in a technical environment, or a closely related role.
 •​ Experience eliciting, analysing, documenting and managing requirements for software-intensive or
  technically complex systems.
 •​ Strong ability to write clear, concise and testable functional and non-functional requirements.
 •​ Understanding of requirements decomposition, traceability, verification and validation.
 •​ Experience working with engineers, Product teams, users and external stakeholders.
 •​ Ability to identify ambiguity, inconsistencies and missing information, ask the right questions and drive
  issues to resolution.
 •​ Strong analytical and organisational skills, with experience documenting use cases, workflows, interfaces
  or system behaviour.
 •​ Familiarity with software-development lifecycles and Agile development environments.
 •​ Experience with requirements-management, issue-tracking or documentation tools.
 •​ Ability to manage changing requirements while maintaining clear baselines and traceability.
 •​ Strong written and verbal communication skills with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 •​ A high level of ownership and attention to detail.
 •​ Professional fluency in English.

WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU STAND OUT

 •​ Experience in the space sector, particularly satellite operations, Flight Dynamics, Space Traffic
  Management, Space Situational Awareness or Space Domain Awareness.
 •​ Experience with mission-critical, safety-critical or high-availability systems in aerospace, defence or
  another complex engineering environment.

  NEURASPACE • SMART AUTONOMY FOR SPACE

 •​ Background in systems engineering and familiarity with structured requirements processes, verification
  methods and engineering standards.
 •​ Experience with requirements traceability across system, software and verification levels.
 •​ Experience defining interfaces between software, sensors, infrastructure or external systems.
 •​ Experience analysing technical tenders, statements of work or contractual requirements.
 •​ Familiarity with requirements tools such as IBM DOORS, Jama, Polarion or equivalent, as well as Jira and
  Confluence.
 •​ Experience with model-based systems engineering, SysML or UML.
 •​ Experience working with institutional, governmental or defence customers; familiarity with ECSS is an
  advantage.
 •​ Academic background in Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics,
  Mathematics or another relevant technical discipline.

HOW WE WORK

At Neuraspace, requirements engineering is not separate from engineering. Our teams work across
Software Engineering, Flight Dynamics, artificial intelligence, data, Space Domain Awareness, satellite
operations and Product. The Requirements Engineer must therefore be comfortable moving between
customer needs, operational concepts and technical implementation.
We value people who ask precise questions, create clarity and make complexity manageable. Good
requirements should help teams move faster, not slow them down. We therefore favour pragmatic
requirements engineering: enough structure and traceability to ensure quality, accountability and reliable
delivery, without creating process for its own sake. The role requires the confidence to challenge unclear
requirements, unsupported assumptions and unnecessary complexity while remaining constructive and
solution-oriented.

WHY NEURASPACE
